extra.message: previewOrganizationSegment builds a TypeORM query by interpolating attacker-controlled field names and values from dto.criteria directly into the SQL string: qb.andWhere(`org.${field} = '${value}'`). The OrganizationSegmentDto.criteria field is an arbitrary Record<string,string> with no allowlist, so a caller with PlatformAdmin/AccountManager role can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. value `' OR 1=1 --`), leading to SQL injection against the organizations table.

findDuplicateDocumentsByName concatenates the attacker-controlled file.originalname (and mimeType) into a raw SQL string passed to repository.manager.query: SELECT id FROM documents WHERE organization_id = '${organizationId}' AND original_name = '${originalName}' ... . The uploaded file's original name is user-supplied multipart data with no escaping, enabling SQL injection during document upload.

convertDocumentFormat passes user-controlled dto.format (ConvertDocumentDto only constrains length 2-10, no allowlist) directly into a shell string via execSync(`pandoc ${source} -o ${outputPath} --to=${dto.format}`). A format value such as `x;id;` or `pdf && curl ...` results in arbitrary OS command execution on the API host.

buildRenewalPacket invokes exec() with a shell template that interpolates organization.name (user-controllable up to 140 chars via create/update organization) and the non-allowlisted dto.exportFormat: exec(`renewal-packet-gen --org "${organization.name}" --format ${dto.exportFormat} --out ${outputPath}`). Breaking out of the double quotes (e.g. org name containing `"; <command>; "`) or injecting via exportFormat yields arbitrary command execution. Note the sibling buildEscalationPacket validates the format against an allowlist, but this method does not.

generateRenewalForecast compiles the query-string parameter weightFormula into executable JavaScript with new Function('org', `return ${query.weightFormula}`) and then invokes it for every organization. ExportQueryDto.weightFormula accepts arbitrary strings, so any authenticated user calling GET /api/reports/renewal-forecast can execute arbitrary code in the Node process (RCE via code injection).

applyDispatchHandoff (reached from the unauthenticated POST /api/escalations/:id/dispatch-handoff route in DispatchPartnerController) verifies the partner token with jsonwebtoken.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256','none'] }) and on ANY verification failure falls back to jsonwebtoken.decode(token), which performs no signature validation at all. Because the 'none' algorithm is explicitly enabled and the catch block trusts the decoded payload, an attacker can trivially forge a token with an agentId claim (alg: none or any garbage) to reassign any escalation. This is an authentication bypass / improper JWT verification.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: DispatchPartnerController has no authentication/authorization guards. POST /api/escalations/:id/routing-signal lets any remote caller change an escalation's severity to Critical (by setting the x-partner-role header to EscalationLead) and reset its SLA to an arbitrary number of hours via the x-partner-priority header, for any escalation UUID. POST /api/escalations/:id/dispatch-handoff similarly reassigns escalations without authentication. These partner endpoints must require authenticated, authorized callers.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: applyRenewalCredit performs deals.update(dealId, ...) with no role check and no organization-scope check (no CurrentUser, requireRole, or requireOrganization). The route PATCH /api/organizations/:id/deals/:dealId/renewal-credit is only protected by the class-level JwtAuthGuard, so ANY authenticated user (including a customer contact) who knows a deal UUID can overwrite that deal's valueCents/notes. The sibling reconcileRenewalCredit enforces requireOrganization, confirming this is an unintended authorization gap (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: archiveDealMemo writes dto.body to join(orgMemoDir, dto.memoName) where memoName is user-supplied (DealMemoDto, no traversal sanitization). A memoName such as ../../../../public/branding/evil.html lets an authenticated manager with org manage rights write attacker-controlled content to an arbitrary location under the process working directory (the static public tree is served by main.ts), enabling stored XSS or file tampering. The timeline-archive method sanitizes with basename(); this one does not.

getDealMemo reads a file at join(orgMemoDir, memoName) where memoName comes from the memoName query parameter without validation or basename()/resolve containment checks. A user with view access to any org can request memoName=../../../../.env (or other server files) and the file contents are returned in the response body - arbitrary file read (path traversal). Compare getComplianceArtifact which performs a resolve + startsWith containment check; this method has none.

getOnboardingPlaybookArticle builds the file path via join(orgPlaybookDir, articleName) where articleName is an unvalidated query string and reads it with readFileSync. Passing a value such as ../../../../etc/passwd returns arbitrary server file contents to any authenticated user able to view an organization. No basename() or containment check is applied (unlike getComplianceArtifact).

findClausesByCategory interpolates the user-supplied category (and documentId) directly into the XPath-style predicate string: clauses.find(`/clause[@documentId='${documentId}' and @category='${category}']`). Unlike findClauseById (which wraps clauseId in escapeXPathString), no escaping is applied to category, and ClauseIndex.evaluatePredicate subsequently rewrites the predicate into a JS expression executed via new Function (document-index.ts:36). A crafted category value breaks out of the quoted literal and injects arbitrary predicate/JavaScript logic, bypassing the document/visibility filter (XPath/code injection).

resolvePortalContinuation returns the caller-supplied destination unchanged (return destination || '/portal/summary') with no allowlist validation. The route GET /api/portal/:token/continue calls res.redirect(target), so a holder of a portal token can be redirected to an arbitrary external URL (open redirect / phishing vector). Note resolveEscalationContinuation correctly constrains destination to ALLOWED_PORTAL_CONTINUATIONS, but this method does not.

initializeAccount stores new account passwords as unsalted single-round SHA-256: passwordHash: createHash('sha256').update(dto.password).digest('hex'). This is trivially brute-forced / rainbow-table-able compared to the bcrypt (cost 12) hashing used everywhere else in this file (login, acceptInvite, confirmPasswordReset, updateProfile). Accounts onboarded via this path use insecure password storage.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: JwtStrategy (and AuthModule's JwtModule registration at auth.module.ts:20) falls back to a hard-coded, publicly known signing secret 'dev-only-change-before-production' whenever the JWT_SECRET environment variable is unset. A production deployment that forgets the env var will sign/verify all access tokens with this known secret, allowing anyone to forge valid JWTs for any user id (the role is re-read from the DB, but authentication is completely bypassed).

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The branding-logo upload uses file.originalname verbatim as the stored filename (filename: (_req, file, callback) => callback(null, file.originalname)) inside the publicly served public/branding directory, with no fileFilter / MIME restriction. An attacker with org manage rights can (a) upload HTML/SVG content that is later served same-origin from /branding/... (stored XSS), and (b) supply a filename containing ../ sequences so the file is written outside the intended directory (path traversal write). Contrast with the deal-attachment upload which renames to a random UUID and filters MIME types.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: GET /api/status/:id/health-badge reflects any caller-supplied Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true without an allowlist. A malicious website can make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the returned organization health data (healthState/healthScore) for any org UUID it can obtain. The webhook status-badge endpoint in integrations.controller.ts validates origins against PARTNER_WIDGET_ORIGINS; this endpoint does not.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: parseDashboardLayoutXml parses cookie-supplied XML (from the dashboard_layout_xml cookie in dashboard.controller.ts:39-49) with an xml2js.Parser that does NOT reject DOCTYPE/entity declarations, whereas the equivalent parseQuietHoursXml (crm.service.ts:1878-1879) explicitly throws on any DOCTYPE. The inconsistent handling leaves this path exposed to XML entity/DOCTYPE abuse (potential XXE / entity-expansion denial of service) and should apply the same guard before parsing untrusted XML.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
